title: P9 reliability gates: worker crash recovery (REL-001), classroom queue load test (REL-002), deployment security controls (REL-003)

REL-001_worker_recovers_from_crash.statement: REAL process death (SIGKILL mid-solve) followed by restart on the same SQLite store: the interrupted job re-queued and completed, no stuck 'running' rows remained, no orphan result versions were published, idempotency keys were honored after restart, and store migrations were idempotent across double reopen.
REL-001_worker_recovers_from_crash.method: Child process (subprocess with the worktree on PYTHONPATH) boots the real create_app + JobRunner with a SleepingSolver that sleeps 30 s mid-solve. The parent polls the SQLite store read-only (file: URI mode=ro) until the job row is 'running', then SIGKILLs the child. The frozen 'running' row is asserted on disk, the store is reopened twice (migration idempotence, schema_version == LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION both times), the app is restarted in-process on the SAME state_root with a fast solver, and the recovery invariants are asserted end to end.
invariants_verified: interrupted job re-queued by JobRunner.start() start-up recovery and completed after restart (exactly one solver call in the restarted process)
nonterminal_jobs() == [] after recovery — no stuck 'running'/'queued' rows
scene_version == exact_result_version == 1; result_versions == [0, 1] with checksums matching the published manifests — no orphan versions
idempotency replay: same Idempotency-Key + same body returns 202 with the same job_id; same key + different body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused
store migrations idempotent across two reopens (schema_version stable)
REL-001_worker_recovers_from_crash.recovery_hole_found: none — the existing JobRunner.start() start-up requeue of nonterminal durable jobs already covers hard crash; no production code fix was required for recovery

REL-002_classroom_queue_load.statement: Real-time classroom-shaped load test with the REAL solver (default ExactWorker) on the tests' synthetic tiny site: every accepted edit reached a terminal status (none silently dropped), the queue fully drained, every scenario ended exact at its latest scene version, bursts coalesced (superseded > 0), and steady-state queue-wait p95 stayed within 2x service time. Wall clock 186.2 s, under the 600 s mission budget.

fixture.solver: default make_exact_worker_solver (ExactWorker), real physics, no fake latency

calibration.basis: testing_validation.md 'Queue load test' (20 scenarios, 1 edit/120 s, bursts of 5 in 10 s, 1 worker) scaled to the mission's <10 min wall budget by keeping the ARRIVAL/SERVICE RATIO at the spec's ~4.8 (measured 120/25 s from P8) and compressing the service time via the tiny fixture; 10 scenarios instead of 20 keeps >= 8 required by the mission

REL-002_classroom_queue_load.note: Superseded jobs are burst coalescing, not dropped edits: each burst of 5 within ~2 s coalesced to one completing job (4 superseded + 1 complete per burst) and every scenario's final scene version has an exact published result. Steady p95 wait 3.988 s vs 2x measured service 6.884 s.

REL-003_security_controls.statement: Deployment security controls implemented in-app with stdlib/FastAPI only (no new dependencies), all default-ON and configurable via create_app parameters: request body limit (413), per-IP sliding-window rate limit plus per-scenario edit budget (429 + Retry-After), tree count/property bounds enforcement (403/422), and the reverse-proxy TLS termination model (uvicorn --proxy-headers) proven over real HTTP.

request_body_limit.behavior: Content-Length precheck before reading the body, then actual-size check after read (chunked bodies covered); responses/exports never throttled

per_ip_rate_limit.caveat: in-process sliding window; multi-process/public deployments need a proxy-level limiter (documented with the reverse-proxy snippets)

tree_bounds.single_source: solweig_gpu/incremental/trees.py TREE_HEIGHT_RANGE_M / TREE_CANOPY_DIAMETER_RANGE_M and TreeSpec validation; the server routes call the same validator so server and library can never disagree

tls_termination.model: reverse proxy terminates TLS; uvicorn --proxy-headers + --forwarded-allow-ips lets the app rate-limit by the real client from X-Forwarded-For
tls_termination.proof: tests/test_deployment_smoke.py boots uvicorn with proxy_headers=True and shows distinct X-Forwarded-For clients get distinct rate budgets while the direct client exhausts its own
tls_termination.snippets: docs/incremental_design_tool/benchmarks/2026-09-02-p9-reliability/reverse_proxy_tls.md (Caddy + nginx incl. SSE proxy_buffering off / X-Accel-Buffering)

notes_for_doc_reconciliation: create_app default max_trees_per_scenario=200 predates this phase; deployment_operations.md suggests SOLWEIG_MAX_TREES_PER_SCENARIO=100. The code default is unchanged here (no scientific basis claimed to move it); deployments should set it explicitly to the documented 100 if that is the intended classroom cap.

deployment_operations.md 'Security controls' list (request body limit, per-IP/per-scenario rate limits, tree bounds, HTTPS) is now fully implemented server-side; the doc's prose needs no change but can cite these parameters.
models.py documents trunk_ratio as [0, 1) (library-authoritative); data_model.md still says [0, 1] — flagged for the lead, unchanged here.

T6_deployment_smoke.statement: Boots the FastAPI app under a REAL uvicorn server on an ephemeral port (temp store + synthetic cache with real .npy bytes, gated fake solver) and drives the full deployment-critical path over HTTP: /health/live, /health/ready (store/sites/worker/result_fs checks), /health/worker diagnostics, create scenario, post edit with Idempotency-Key, SSE event stream (job-progress + result-ready), result manifest, binary payload with BOTH Accept encodings (zstd + identity) with per-encoding checksum/ETag verification and 304 conditional GET, patch_codec decodability of both encodings, and scenario reset. Second test runs a tight security profile + proxy headers.
